overview.one_line: Built an NLP-based cyberbullying detection system that classifies harmful social media content into multiple bullying categories using machine learning models and ensemble techniques.
overview.summary: Cyberbullying Detection is an NLP project developed as part of an academic Natural Language Processing course. The system analyzes social media text and identifies whether content contains cyberbullying behavior. The project uses traditional NLP preprocessing techniques, feature engineering, and multiple machine learning algorithms including Logistic Regression, SVM, Naive Bayes, Random Forest, and XGBoost. An ensemble approach was used to improve classification performance across multiple cyberbullying categories.
overview.elevator_pitch: An NLP-powered cyberbullying detection system that analyzes social media posts and classifies harmful content into multiple bullying categories with approximately 90% accuracy.

problem.statement: Cyberbullying has become increasingly common across social media platforms, causing emotional, psychological, and social harm. Manual moderation is difficult due to the large volume of user-generated content.
problem.why_it_matters: Automated cyberbullying detection systems can assist content moderation, improve online safety, and help identify harmful behavior at scale.

motivation.why_i_built_it: The project was developed as part of my Natural Language Processing coursework while exploring practical applications of machine learning and text classification.
motivation.personal_interest: I wanted to gain hands-on experience with text preprocessing, feature extraction, machine learning pipelines, and ensemble modeling techniques using real-world social media data.
project_goals: Improve classification accuracy through ensemble methods

architecture.v1: The initial implementation focused on traditional NLP preprocessing and individual machine learning models trained independently on the dataset.
architecture.v2: Multiple algorithms including Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, SVM, Decision Trees, Random Forest, and XGBoost were evaluated and compared.
architecture.current: The current architecture preprocesses tweets using NLTK-based NLP techniques, extracts features using TF-IDF, and applies an ensemble approach combining multiple machine learning models. Predictions from the strongest-performing models are combined to improve classification accuracy across six cyberbullying categories.
architecture.future: Future versions could support multilingual cyberbullying detection, regional language processing, social media platform integrations, and deep learning transformer-based architectures.

implementation_journey.initial_approach: The project started as a text classification problem using traditional NLP preprocessing and supervised machine learning algorithms.
major_milestones: Evaluated classification performance across multiple categories.
key_decisions: Use traditional machine learning instead of deep learning.
Compare multiple algorithms rather than relying on a single model.
Use ensemble prediction to improve accuracy.
Focus on category-level classification instead of binary detection.

challenges.solution: Evaluated multiple machine learning algorithms and compared their performance.
challenges.lesson: Different algorithms perform differently depending on dataset characteristics.

challenges.solution: Used multi-class classification instead of simple binary detection.
challenges.lesson: Real-world moderation requires more granular classification.

challenges.solution: Combined outputs from multiple high-performing models using ensemble techniques.
challenges.lesson: Ensemble methods can outperform individual classifiers.

results.current_status: Completed academic NLP project available through GitHub and Jupyter Notebook implementation.
technical_outcomes: Trained on a dataset containing over 10,000 social media posts.
Classified content into six cyberbullying categories.
Evaluated Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Decision Trees.
Achieved approximately 90% classification accuracy using ensemble methods.
project_highlights: Focused on practical social media moderation use cases.

lessons_learned: Traditional machine learning remains highly effective for many NLP classification tasks.
Feature engineering significantly impacts model performance.
Ensemble models can improve predictive accuracy.
Data preprocessing is one of the most important stages of NLP pipelines.
Multi-class classification provides more actionable outputs than binary classification.
future_improvements: Handle transliterated text such as Telugu or Hindi written using English characters.
Integrate with social media platforms such as Instagram and Twitter.

architecture_decisions.decision: Used traditional machine learning algorithms instead of deep learning.
architecture_decisions.reason: Provided strong performance while remaining interpretable and efficient.
Produced higher accuracy than individual models.
Provided more meaningful outputs than simple bullying versus non-bullying classification.
